title: Machine Vision-Based Defect Detection for Automotive Brake Pads: A Review of System Components, Image Processing Methods, and Applications
abstract: Automotive brake pads are safety-critical components whose manufacturing quality directly affects braking reliability. Manual inspection is inefficient and susceptible to subjective judgment, whereas machine vision provides a non-contact and automated solution for defect detection. This article reviews machine vision-based inspection of automotive brake pads from three perspectives: system components, image processing methods, and industrial applications. The reviewed technologies include image acquisition hardware, conventional image processing, machine learning, deep learning, and their applications to contour, surface, character, and dimensional inspection. Existing methods are compared in terms of detection capability, interpretability, data dependence, computational cost, environmental robustness, and deployment suitability.The literature shows that conventional image processing remains effective under stable imaging conditions, while deep learning offers stronger feature representation and adaptability but requires representative datasets and greater computing resources. Current challenges include limited public datasets, inconsistent evaluation protocols, sensitivity to industrial variations, and the trade-off between accuracy and real-time performance. Future research should emphasize standardized datasets, lightweight models, few-shot learning, multimodal sensing, and integration with intelligent manufacturing systems. title: ON THE CALCULATION OF BRAKING TORQUES IN DRUM SHOE BRAKE MECHANISMS
abstract: Friction brakes generate braking torque through the friction force between rotating (disk, drum) and non-rotating (pad, band) components.Drum-type brakes are primarily used in heavy-duty vehicles.To initiate braking, the shoe is pressed against the drum, creating contact pressure between the pressed surfaces.Tangential stresses arising from drum rotation produce the braking torque.The braking torque in the brake mechanism depends on the contact pressure and the coefficient of friction between the compressed surfaces.With a large compressive force, the deformations of the drum and shoe differ, altering the drum's round cross-section and causing variations in braking force at different moments.Therefore, accurately determining contact pressure is crucial for drum brakes.This article focuses on calculating braking torque by determining the deformations of the mold as close to real-world conditions as possible.

title: Effects of Different Transition Metal Oxide Mineral Dusts on Secondary Organic Aerosol Photochemistry
abstract: Abstract Secondary organic aerosols (SOA) can undergo photochemical aging upon solar irradiation, changing their physical and chemical properties. Mineral dust particles internally mixed with SOA may act as a heterogeneous photocatalytic surface, altering the photochemical aging processes available to SOA compounds and changing their overall composition. We examined aqueous photodegradation of laboratory-generated α-pinene ozonolysis SOA in the presence of α-Fe2O3 (hematite), TiO2 (anatase), Arizona test dust (AZTD), and automotive ceramic brake pad dust. Anatase, a well-known photocatalyst, accelerated the photodegradation of SOA as expected. While hematite did not display the photocatalytic properties of anatase, its presence in solution did change the distribution of photoproducts for select SOA compounds such as cis-pinonic acid. Arizona test dust and brake wear dust behaved more similarly to hematite than anatase, displaying low photocatalytic activity but subtly changing the distribution of photodegradation products.

title: Long-Term Characterization of Non-Exhaust Particulate Concentrations at Two Contrasting Near-Road Sites: Source Contributions and Real-World Emission Factors
abstract: Abstract As exhaust emissions (EE) from motor vehicles decline, non-exhaust emissions (NEE) from brake wear (BW), tire wear, and road dust (RD) are becoming a major source of traffic-related particulate matter (PM). Hence, there is a pressing need to characterize the resulting exposures and health burden. Here we examine the factors affecting NEE concentrations in ambient fine and coarse PM (PM2.5 and PM10–2.5) using speciated PM measurements conducted near a highway and an arterial road in Canada. Receptor model source apportionment analysis showed BW and RD combined contributed 28–49% of traffic-derived PM2.5, with associated near-road concentrations being 4–8 times higher for PM10–2.5 than PM2.5. Copper and iron, primarily contributed by BW, were 2–5 times higher than background levels. Multiple linear regression analysis showed NEE concentrations are affected by meteorology, traffic volume, and fleet composition. Emission factor (EF) calculations showed copper emission per vehicle-kilometer traveled declined at a rate of 7–9% year–1 (p < 0.001), cautioning against its use as a stable BW marker as brake pad formulations evolve. While the EFs for EE were comparable across both sites due to similar heavy-duty vehicle (HDV) shares, BW and RD EFs were 3–4 times higher at the highway site, highlighting driving conditions as key determinants of NEE emissions. title: SOLUTION OF THE THERMOELASTIC PROBLEM IN THE DRUM-SHOE CONTACT IN A BRAKE MECHANISM
abstract: During braking, the temperature of drum brakes can reach 300-350°C, which changes the coefficient of friction between the lining and the drum, causing the braking torque to fluctuate.The actual values of the braking torque, as well as the deformation of the shoe and drum, depend on the contact pressure, the temperature regime of the contacting surfaces, and their strength characteristics.Knowing the actual values of the contact pressure allows one to determine the deformation values; conversely, knowing the deformation values makes it possible to determine the contact pressure.On contacting surfaces, deformation can be represented by two components: elastic and thermoelastic deformation.Given the rigidity and strength properties, geometric dimensions of the brake mechanism elements, and the forces acting on the contact surfaces, it is possible to calculate the deformation values and contact stresses during braking.This article addresses the problem of determining thermoelastic deformations in order to calculate the braking torque of drum brake mechanisms.

title: Engineering of Tire Tread Patterns : Mechanics, Materials, Design Methodology and Performance Optimization — a comprehensive framework from rubber contact mechanics and friction physics to wet traction, noise, wear, rolling resistance,
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The pneumatic tire is the single point of contact between a vehicle and the road, and its tread pattern constitutes the engineered interface through which microscopic material interactions are translated into macroscopic vehicle behavior. This thesis develops a comprehensive engineering framework for the design, analysis, and optimization of tire tread patterns, grounded in the contact mechanics of viscoelastic solids, the physics of rubber friction, and the fluid dynamics of water evacuation. The work integrates three levels of description. At the molecular and microscopic scales, viscoelastic energy dissipation and adhesive interactions generate friction. At the mesoscopic scale, road asperity geometry and tread block compliance determine the real area of contact. At the macroscopic scale, groove networks, sipe density, and block geometry govern water drainage, hydroplaning resistance, noise emission, wear life, and rolling resistance. A systematic synthesis of more than six decades of peer-reviewed research, ranging from Grosch's foundational work on the relationship between friction and viscoelastic loss spectra to Persson's contact mechanics theory and contemporary finite element and machine learning approaches, is combined with an engineering methodology articulated through design rules, worked examples, and decision frameworks. title: Noncontact friction of a semiconductor with charge carriers of differing mobilities
abstract: The coefficient of noncontact friction as measured in an electric force microscopy experiment is computed for a semiconductor with positive and negative charge carriers of distinct mobilities. The friction is determined for a sample represented by classical electrodynamics coupled to diffusing carriers in a dielectric continuum. The analysis generalizes previous work in which positive and negative carriers were taken to have identical mobilities, allowing application to a wider range of semiconductors. Dielectric and electrical properties of the material are shown to be revealed by the dependence of the friction on experimentally accessible parameters such as probe-sample separation and carrier density.

title: Trade Facilitation and the Redistribution of Cross-Border Logistics Friction: Evidence from Peru
abstract: Background: Single windows, customs risk management, authorized economic operator (AEO) programs and port community systems are expected to lower cross-border logistics friction. Evidence on how much friction they remove is abundant; evidence on where the surviving friction settles, and who absorbs it, is scarce. Peru, with mature facilitation instruments yet weak logistics performance, is the case examined. Methods: Twenty sessions—thirteen institutional interviews and seven roundtables and workshops with border agencies, port, airport, warehouse and postal operators and exporter associations (2611 speaker turns, 137,984 words)—were analyzed through codebook thematic analysis with two coding rounds, a negative-case search and intercoder verification (κ = 0.881 for codability, 0.824 aggregate). Results: Facilitation did not eliminate friction but redistributed it along three coupled pathways: institutional (the digital instrument stops at each agency’s boundary), material (digital coordination runs on nodes whose physical capacity nobody coordinates) and segment-based (trust devices reward operators who already comply). Six node-level mechanisms are documented, and predictability proved codable (κ = 0.712) and concerned decisions more than durations. Conclusions: The Friction Redistribution Framework is proposed as a diagnostic and a set of grounded hypotheses: for each instrument, where residual friction lands, who absorbs it and which indicator would reveal it.

title: Analyzing Mild Steel Surface Process Parameters Using Friction Stir Processing
journal: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
abstract: Marine infrastructure includes docks and piers, offshore oil rigs, and shipbuilding (hulls, decks, and superstructures) all make extensive use of mild steel. When combined with appropriate protective coatings or cathodic protection, its high tensile strength, exceptional weldability, ductility, and affordability make it a top option even if its low carbon content makes it vulnerable to corrosion in saltwater. By producing a refined, uniform microstructure without melting the material, Friction Stir Processing (FSP) enhances the surface characteristics of mild steel. The present investigations involve the simulation study of friction stir processing. The study is done to analyse the surface morphology and process parameters involves in friction stir processing. The simulations are performed with 100 N force and 52.36 rad/ sec and the output parameters like deformation, shear stress and shear strain were calculated. The results found were suitable and useful for the further study.

title: An efficient method for accounting the strength-differential effect and Coulomb friction in upper bound solutions of plasticity
abstract: The upper bound method is widely used to estimate the load required to deform the material in metal forming processes. However, most solutions are for the von Mises or Tresca yield criteria. It may be explained by the simplicity with which the plastic work rate is expressed in terms of the strain rate invariants when these criteria are adopted. Therefore, it is more convenient to formulate the constitutive equations using the work function. If necessary, the latter can usually be chosen to closely approximate available yield criteria. The strength-differential effect is an important property of some materials whose plastic yielding is independent of the state of hydrostatic stress. In this paper, a recently proposed work function appropriate for such materials is combined with the upper bound technique. As an example, the upsetting of a cylinder, which is sometimes used as a friction test, is analyzed. Coulomb’s friction law is assumed between the plates and the cylinder, which requires a non-conventional formulation of the upper bound theorem. The solution is compared to that for the von Mises yield criterion. It is shown that neglecting the strength-differential effect in the material model can affect the interpretation of the friction test.

title: Effects of Pavement Surface Texture and Interfacial Friction on Tire Rolling Resistance: A Finite Element Study
abstract: To investigate the effects of pavement textures and tire–pavement interfacial friction on tire rolling resistance, a three-dimensional tire–pavement rolling finite element model was developed considering flat, arc-shaped, triangular, and rectangular textures under different friction coefficient conditions (μ = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8). The effects of textures and μ on tire–pavement contact responses, energy dissipation, and rolling resistance were analyzed, and the rolling resistance coefficient (Crr) was calculated based on energy dissipation theory. Furthermore, scaled rolling resistance tests were conducted under different pavement surface materials to validate the trends obtained from finite element simulations. The results show that pavement textures significantly affect tire–pavement contact responses under rigid pavement conditions. Compared with the flat texture, the triangular texture increases the contact length and peak contact pressure by approximately 18.9% and 458.1%, respectively, indicating enhanced contact pressure concentration. Compared with rigid pavement, flexible pavement structural deformation further influences tire–pavement contact responses and extends the deformation region. The arc-shaped texture exhibits more pronounced deformation responses and higher energy dissipation. title: Performance of Cr 3 C 2 -Ti-DLC coated tools in dissimilar friction stir welding
abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) is an effective joining approach for dissimilar base metals, such as aluminum alloys (AA) and advanced high-strength steels. However, tool degradation during the process can compromise weld quality, shorten tool life, and increase production costs. This study evaluates the performance and durability enhancement of the tool through the FSW of AA6022-T4 and galvanized DP600 steel by applying Cr 3 C 2 -Ti-DLC thin-film coatings on H13 tool steel and WC-10% Co tools. The surface finish quality of the welds was quantitatively evaluated using a 3D white light interferometer, while real-time thermal profiles were captured using an infrared thermography camera. Tool degradation patterns and performance were assessed through optical microscopy, SEM coupled with EDS, and precise weight loss measurements. The uncoated H13 tool exhibited significant degradation, including thread flattening, micro-abrasion, and material pickup. In contrast, the uncoated WC-10% Co tool demonstrated improved wear resistance. The deposition of thin-film surface coatings significantly reduced tool degradation by 26% for H13 and 23% for WC-10% Co tools in comparison with uncoated tools. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of thin-film surface coatings in improving tool performance and durability, particularly in dissimilar material friction stir welding.

title: Process structure property correlation and multi response optimization of friction stir welded copper joints
abstract: Abstract Friction stir welding (FSW) of copper is challenging due to its high thermal conductivity, which complicates heat management and joint integrity. This study investigates the process–structure–property relationship in FSW of 5 mm thick commercially pure copper plates using a conventional vertical milling machine as a cost-effective alternative to dedicated FSW systems. In contrast, tool geometry primarily governs hardness (84.67% contribution, p < 0.001) through its role in strain distribution and dynamic recrystallization, with a maximum hardness of 94 HRE obtained using the square pin profile at 910 RPM and 44 mm/min (S7). title: Substantiation of the Design and Operating Parameters of a Vibro-Friction Separator with a Preliminary Separation Device for Small-Seeded Oil Crops
abstract: The article presents the scientific results on the design and operating parameters of a vibro-friction separator for separating small-seeded oil crops. The relevance of the study is in the complexity of cleaning and fractionating small-seeded crops, whose physical and mechanical properties exhibit considerable variability in shape, size, mass, elasticity, and friction. The use of vibro-friction separation enables differences in these properties; however, its efficiency largely depends on how the material is fed onto the working surfaces. The study aims to improve the separation efficiency of small-seed mixtures by substantiating the design and operating parameters of a vibro-friction separator equipped with a preliminary separation device. A separator design incorporating a screw feeder was proposed, in which the working surfaces provided a preliminary spatial distribution of the seed mixture components based on their physical and mechanical properties. Numerical simulation and experimental methods were employed to investigate the separation process. The effects of vibration amplitude and frequency, as well as the directional, longitudinal, and transverse inclination angles of the working surface, on separation quality, throughput, and power consumption were determined. title: Compensation of Linear Misalignments in EN AW-6082-T6 Aluminium Sheets by Multi-Pin Wire-Based Friction Stir Welding
journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
abstract: Linear misalignment (LM) can arise from dimensional tolerances, positioning inaccuracies, limited component stiffness, and clamping constraints, particularly in large-scale welded structures. While filler-assisted fusion welding provides some flexibility for accommodating such geometrical deviations, conventional friction stir welding (FSW) relies on direct tool–workpiece contact and a fixed pin geometry, making pronounced out-of-plane deviations particularly challenging. This study investigates the compensation of severe LM by multi-pin wire-based friction stir welding (W-FSW) of 2 mm thick EN AW-6082-T6 aluminium sheets using continuously supplied EN AW-6082 filler wire. LM values of 1.0 and 1.5 mm, corresponding to 50% and 75% of the base material thickness, were introduced with the elevated sheet positioned on either the advancing or retreating side. Welding without filler material resulted in pronounced bonding defects and lack of penetration. In contrast, continuous filler-material supply enabled all investigated LM configurations to be compensated and resulted in substantially improved joint consolidation. Tensile strengths between 198.8 and 210.0 MPa were achieved, compared with 208.71 MPa for a reference W-FSW joint without LM. journal: Journal of Railway Transportation and Technology
abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) is a solid-state joining process that is increasingly used to fabricate aluminum railway carbodies. This study examined the effect of tool pin diameter on the tensile properties of FSW joints in 6 mm thick AA6061-T6 aluminum plates. High-speed steel tools with a 13 mm flat shoulder and straight cylindrical pins of 3, 4, and 5 mm diameter were fabricated by turning, and butt joints were welded on a conventional milling machine at a rotational speed of 1130 rpm, a traverse speed of 20 mm/min, and a tilt angle of 3°. Three joints were produced for each pin diameter (n = 3), and one transverse tensile specimen was tested from each joint. Results are reported as mean ± standard deviation and were analyzed using one-way ANOVA, the Kruskal–Wallis test, and Spearman’s rank correlation. The mean tensile strength decreased from 210.06 ± 5.87 MPa with the 3 mm pin to 190.96 ± 26.57 MPa and 146.36 ± 62.26 MPa with the 4 and 5 mm pins, respectively, while the scatter increased with pin diameter. Owing to the small sample size and large scatter, the differences among group means were not statistically significant (p = 0.206); however, pin diameter was negatively correlated with tensile strength (ρ = −0.74, p = 0.023). Visual inspection revealed less weld flash with the 3 mm pin, consistent with the smaller volume of material displaced by the pin. Within the tested range, the 3 mm pin provided the highest and most consistent tensile strength.

title: Effect of graphite interlayer quantity on weld formation and defect evolution in AA7075–AZ31 dissimilar friction stir welding
abstract: In the present work, AA7075 aluminium alloy and AZ31 magnesium alloy were friction stir welded under three graphite interlayer conditions: 0, 1 and 2 g. All welding trials were conducted using a square-profile HCHCr tool at a rotational speed of 1000 rpm, traverse speed of 15 mm/min and axial force of 2 kN. This study is intended as a preliminary exploratory investigation of the influence of graphite quantity under one fixed processing condition rather than as a process-optimization study. The graphite-free and 2 g graphite conditions did not produce stable bonded regions. In contrast, the 1 g graphite condition generated a comparatively more continuous weld region, although substantial defects remained. FESEM examination of the 1 g condition revealed interfacial discontinuities, void-like regions, crack-like features, fragmented material zones and non-uniform flow structures, demonstrating incomplete consolidation. EDS analysis confirmed the simultaneous presence of Al, Mg and localized carbon-rich regions within the analysed weld zone, indicating partial incorporation of graphite but heterogeneous distribution. Accordingly, the results demonstrate an observed non-monotonic trend in weld formation under the investigated conditions, rather than establishing a universal quantitative relationship between graphite quantity and weld quality. title: Thermo-Mechanical Modeling and Microstructural Evolution in Rotary Friction Welding of AA6061 Aluminum Alloy
abstract: Abstract The current study is concerned with the development and experimental validation of the numerical model for RFW of AA6061 Aluminum alloy using the finite element method (FEM) in ABAQUS/Standard. The main objective is to present an efficient and predictive tool for the optimization of the RFW process to reduce the dependency on costly and time-consuming physical experimentation. The numerical model was developed based on the axisymmetric characteristic of the component, using the coupled thermal-mechanical element CGAX4HT in ABAQUS/Standard. The model incorporates temperature-dependent material properties and high-temperature true stress-strain data. The model validation was performed thoroughly by comparing the simulated results of weld morphology, temperature evolution and axial shortening with experimental data, which showed a good agreement between the numerical predictions and the actual experimental observations. After validation, we used the model to perform a detailed analysis of the distribution of temperature, residual stress, equivalent plastic strain, and strain rate in the weld zone, further establishing, for the first time, a direct quantitative spatial correlation between these simulated thermo-mechanical fields and the experimentally measured boundaries of the dynamically recrystallized zone (DRZ), thermo-mechanically affected zone (TMAZ), and heat-affected zone (HAZ). title: A Cosserat Mohr–Coulomb Model with Isotropic Hardening and Softening of Cohesion, Friction and Dilatancy for Dense Sand: Laboratory Calibration and Strip-Footing Analyses
abstract: Dense sands exhibit pressure-dependent peak strength, dilatancy and post-peak softening, which can cause mesh-sensitive strain localization in conventional displacement-based finite element analyses. This study develops a plane-strain Cosserat Mohr–Coulomb model with a Rankine tension cut-off and evolving cohesion, friction and dilatancy. A multi-surface return algorithm uses Fischer–Burmeister complementarity, a semismooth Newton solver and a consistent tangent. Material parameters are calibrated using one drained triaxial test on dense Karlsruhe fine sand (100 kPa confinement). Four additional confinement levels (50–400 kPa) are evaluated: with a Bolton-type pressure relation calibrated only at 100 kPa, the largest peak-stress error is 10.5%; refitting its coefficients using all five tests reduces the maximum in-sample error to 3.9%. In rough rigid strip-footing simulations, the near-classical limit develops narrow localized zones and the finer-mesh analysis stops before reaching a peak. Cosserat analyses with l/B=0.025–0.1 complete the loading path on the finer mesh, with peak pressures of 1189–1255 kPa and wedge angles of 59–61∘. A footing-width study further separates the effects of stress-dependent initial stiffness and prescribed internal length. title: Microstructure Evolution of Dissimilar AISI 316L and AISI 444 Stainless Steel Joints by Friction Stir Welding
abstract: Abstract The present study investigated the main microstructural characteristics of dissimilar welding between AISI 316L and AISI 444 stainless steel. In the welds, 25 to 50 kN axial forces were applied, varying the rotation speed between 350 and 450 rpm and keeping the welding speed constant at 1 mm/s. Three types of joint configurations were used: The first type was the butt joint, and the other two types were overlapped joints. Under all conditions, relevant microstructural changes were not observed between base metal (BM) and heat-affected zone (HAZ). In the thermomechanically affected zone (TMAZ) and stir zone (SZ) of the butt joint, the increase in the axial force and the rotational speed shows austenitic and ferritic grains that are poorly refined at the top and more deformed grains with intense refining at the bottom. In the overlap joints, the positioning of AISI 316L steel, with low SFE and easier recrystallisation at the top of the joint, provided a more negligible difference in deformed and recrystallised grains between the upper and lower TMAZ and SZ, where AISI 444 steel is positioned. In none of the welded conditions is it possible to observe areas of excessive grain growth and formation of undesirable phases such as chi, sigma and Laves despite these phases being predicted in the phase diagram of these steels in the temperature range reached in these dissimilar FSW welds. title: Pyrocarbon in shoulder arthroplasty: a narrative review of material properties and summary of clinical outcomes
abstract: Shoulder arthroplasty has seen an exponential increase in the number of procedures performed in the last decade, with numerous implants being introduced into the market. However, the goal of joint preservation remains a major challenge, especially in younger patients where a total joint replacement may be detrimental due to long-term complications. Pyrocarbon was introduced in the shoulder as an alternative to total joint replacement and metallic hemiarthroplasty. Pyrocarbon is a form of carbon which is produced through the pyrolysis of hydrocarbon gases at high temperatures in the absence of oxygen, which results in a material characterized by its isotropy, biocompatibility and low friction properties. It was first used in the human body in mechanical heart valves and then was introduced in orthopaedics to treat various conditions of the hand and wrist. The proposed advantages of pyrocarbon lie in its property of wear resistance and reduced erosion when it is in direct contact with bone and cartilage by virtue of its similar modulus of elasticity to cortical bone. A detailed literature search was carried out to identify the relevant literature available on this topic. In this review, we explore the current state of research and clinical applications of pyrocarbon in shoulder arthroplasty, delving into its mechanical properties, biocompatibility and associated clinical outcomes.

title: Mechanical characterisation of Dendrocalamus asper bamboo and examination of idealised bamboo glulam joints in sustainable materials
abstract: Abstract In this study, mechanical tests are performed on three-year-old Dendrocalamus asper , while the research focuses on conducting an exploratory finite-element study of five idealized bamboo-glulam joints. Compression samples (n = 15) were examined using an adjusted protocol referenced to withdrawn ISO 22157–1:2004; the archived H/D ≈ 2 geometry, deliberate node inclusion, and missing moisture/density records are not equivalent to ISO 22157:2019. Meanwhile, ASTM D3039-type tabbed dog-bone coupons (n = 5) were employed to measure longitudinal tension for practical gripping. However, that composite-material method does not equal the bamboo-specific ISO process. The findings highlighted mean nominal compression and tension strengths of 56.99 and 77.88 MPa, respectively, while the bottom-node group exhibited the highest descriptive compression mean (66.54 MPa). Nonetheless, these findings and not characteristic design values and are not condition-specific. The FE models employ literature-based orthotropy, homogeneous node-free materials, bonded contacts and assumed friction without matched glulam/joint examinations. Meanwhile, model-specific global mesh-sensitivity reruns resulted in adjacent mesh differences of less than 5% in maximum total deformation and equivalent stress at the finest refinement step. title: Analysis of the Effect of Cutting Parameters on Cutting Force and Temperature in Thermo-Mechanical Coupled Orthogonal Cutting of Polyethylene (PE)
journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
abstract: PE material is an ideal type of material for improving corrosion and impact resistance of engineering structural applications, because of its excellent corrosion resistance, low coefficient of friction, and favorable impact resistance. PE structural components generally require precise machining forming in order to satisfy diverse structural and functional requirements. However, PE materials exhibit pronounced temperature sensitivity and thermal softening during the cutting process. The cutting heat generated by plastic deformation and interfacial friction within the cutting zone can significantly influence the local mechanical properties of the material, the cutting-force response, and the resulting surface integrity. This study investigated the cutting mechanism of polyethylene materials through numerical simulation. Based on the mechanical characteristics of PE, a progressive damage constitutive model of the material was defined. Furthermore, a three-dimensional thermo-mechanically coupled cutting model was developed. The accuracy of the proposed model was verified through comparison with previous experimental data. The orthogonal cutting process of polyethylene (PE) was numerically simulated, and the effects of cutting speed and cutting depth on the stress and strain distributions, cutting temperature, and chip formation behavior were systematically analyzed. title: The Effect of Mesh Type and Meshing Strategy on the Finite Element Simulation of a Stack Compression Test
abstract: The stack compression test (SCT) represents an efficient method for characterizing the large deformation behavior of sheet metals and obtaining material parameters for finite element simulations. However, the experimental procedure is affected by several conditions that can lead to uncertainties, particularly regarding the friction conditions between individual specimen layers. Inverse modeling based on finite element simulations offers a potential solution; however, the complex deformation mechanisms within multilayer stacks frequently result in numerical instabilities. Preliminary investigations show that model parameterization strongly influences simulation accountability, while minor variations in friction coefficients may lead to numerical failure. Therefore, this study examines the effects of mesh type and meshing strategy to establish a stable and reliable computational framework for SCT simulations.

title: Mechanical Response and Motion-Mode Dependence of Phonon-Mediated Energy Dissipation in Si–MoS2–Si Sandwich Structure
abstract: Abstract Building on previous studies of monolayer MoS2, this work constructs an atomistic Si–MoS2–Si sandwich structure and investigates its mechanical response and phonon-mediated energy dissipation under interfacial confinement. The tensile results show that the mechanical strength of the sandwich structure gradually decreases as the Si–MoS2 interfacial spacing decreases within the range examined. During fatigue loading, the constraining effect of the Si atomic layers suppresses the out-of-plane deformation of the MoS2 nanosheet and dissipates part of the input energy through lattice vibrations, thereby improving the mechanical stability and fatigue performance of the sandwich structure. However, when fatigue resonance is induced by the external cyclic loading, the central MoS2 nanosheet still fails rapidly. Regarding frictional behavior, two relative motion modes between the upper and lower Si atomic layers and the central MoS2 nanosheet are examined: linear motion and reciprocating motion. Compared with linear motion, reciprocating motion produces a higher degree of phonon-mode matching between the Si atomic layers and the MoS2 nanosheet, facilitating the formation of efficient energy-dissipation pathways and resulting in greater frictional energy dissipation. title: Cr 2 O 3 ‐Mediated Phase Transformation and Microstructural Evolution in LDED CuAlMnTi SMA Coatings Toward Resource‐Efficient Wear Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing the friction‐induced material loss while maintaining the functional response of shape‐memory alloy (SMA) coatings was essential for the resource‐efficient and durable high‐temperature service. In this study, Cr 2 O 3 ‐reinforced CuAlMnTi SMA coatings were fabricated by laser direct energy deposition (LDED), and the composition‐dependent relationships among the microstructural evolution, phase transformation and the high‐temperature tribological performance were systematically investigated. The results show that the introduction of Cr 2 O 3 particles promotes the grain refinement and regulates the phase constitution and transformation behavior of CuAlMnTi SMA matrix, increasing the coating hardness by 9%–44% relative to the substrate. The average coefficients of friction (COFs) and wear rates are decreased with the increase of Cr 2 O 3 content, and the minimal COF and wear rate reach 0.533 and 71.1 ± 3.6 μm 3 ·N −1 ·mm −1 , respectively, demonstrating the friction reduction and wear resistance. The dominant wear mechanisms include adhesive wear, abrasive wear and oxidative wear, which are suppressed by the uniformly distributed Cr 2 O 3 particles and protective oxide films. These findings establish the mechanistic relationship among the Cr 2 O 3 reinforcement, phase transformation and tribological response, providing the viable strategy for the resource‐efficient wear protection and extending the service of SMA‐coated smart structural components. image

title: Financial Ledger as Hyperreality, A Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test: Systemic Decoupling and Physical Limits
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The global financial layer functions increasingly as a hyperreal simulation decoupled from its material baselines. This pre-print deepens the application of a formal diagnostic metric—The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test—to analyze the structural vulnerabilities generated when systemic architectures attempt to bypass biophysical, energetic, and thermodynamic boundaries. Central to this inquiry is an investigation into the system's foundational survival mechanism: it crashes precisely because it was designed with a fatal rule: it was never allowed to know or account for its own imperfections. By substituting real material constraints with advanced epistemic filtering, systemic externalization, and financial virtualization, modern institutions generate an artificial illusion of permanent optimization. This theoretical framework is applied empirically to a contemporary macro-financial case study tracking hidden cross-border capital flows. Through an analysis of U.S. Treasury bond routing, the study reveals how sovereign debt relies on proxy custodian networks in jurisdictions like Canada and Belgium to absorb yield spread differentials and mask geopolitical friction. This mechanism artificially sustains the perceived perfection of the global financial ledger while obscuring underlying systemic concentration and debt-to-GDP friction. title: TRIBOLOGICAL BEHAVIOR OF PVD AND ELECTROPLATED AIRCRAFT COATINGS
abstract: This paper investigates the tribological behavior in sliding friction and the wear resistance of cathodic vacuum-arc (PVD) and electroplated coatings deposited onto high-strength titanium alloy VT-22 and structural steel VKS-170. The relevance of the study is driven by the urgent need to replace environmentally hazardous hard chrome plating with vacuum-arc PVD alternatives, as well as to overcome the high tendency of titanium alloys toward adhesive seizure and galling in aerospace friction units. Face-sliding friction tests were conducted in an AMG-10 aviation hydraulic fluid medium against an AISI 1045 steel counterbody (45–50 HRC). The investigated surface systems included electroplated hard chromium, cathodic vacuum-arc coatings of hard chromium, soft chromium, and molybdenum, as well as uncoated base materials. The experimental findings demonstrate that electroplated chromium exhibits the lowest wear rate. Among the vacuum-arc deposits, hard chromium and molybdenum demonstrate high wear resistance on the VT-22 alloy, which, coupled with exceptional adhesion strength, positions them as viable, eco-friendly substitutes for galvanic chrome plating. title: You are not to know you are imperfect: A Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test A Formal Collaborative Framework on Systemic Decoupling and Physical Limits
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This preprint introduces a formal collaborative framework analyzing the cybernetic imperative of perfection within modern structural networks. The axiom 'You are not to know you are imperfect' serves as a core regulatory vector for modern systems, mandating absolute systemic decoupling from physical, material, and thermodynamic realities. By formalizing this condition via a structured syllogistic critique, we evaluate how modern abstractions—ranging from computational scaling scaling vectors to sovereign debt structures and international treasury flows—maintain operational integrity through the systematic obscuration of friction points. Specifically, we contextualize this framework against recent macroeconomic shifts wherein Chinese trade surpluses seek 'tunnels' via Canadian-domiciled custodial accounts to access the U.S. bond market. We conclude that systemic decoupling functions as a temporary regulatory bridge that accelerates toward systemic rupture when operational resource demands collide irreversibly with the invariant physical boundaries of the material substrate.

title: Share Issues vs. Share Repurchases
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences
abstract: Almost all firms repurchase shares through open-market repurchase programs. In contrast, issue methods are more diverse; at-the-market offerings, analogous to open-market repurchases, and seasoned equity offerings, analogous to rarely used tender-offer repurchases, are both used by significant fractions of firms. Furthermore, average seasoned equity offerings are larger than at-the-market offerings. We show that this asymmetry in the diversity of transaction methods in issuances and repurchases and the size-method relation in issuances are natural consequences of the single informational friction of a firm having superior information to investors. Moreover, although this friction always leads firms to issue inefficiently little, it leads firms to repurchase too little if they maximize long-term shareholder value but too much if the primary goal is to boost short-term share prices. title: A composite treatment method for improving the tribological properties of GCr15 by combining ultrasonic shot peening and surface texturing
abstract: GCr15 bearing steel suffers from severe wear failure under high-speed, heavy-load and thin-oil lubrication conditions, limiting the service reliability of transmission components in aerospace, weaponry and engineering machinery. Surface texturing and shot peening have been widely adopted to improve the tribological performance of metallic materials. Nevertheless, single surface texturing inevitably causes interfacial discontinuity and stress concentration, restricting its wear-resistance improvement. Similarly, conventional shot peening effectively enhances surface hardness and wear resistance via plastic deformation, yet it fails to regulate interfacial lubrication and friction behavior. To address these limitations, this work investigates a composite treatment combining ultrasonic shot peening (USP) and surface micro-texturing, with particular attention to the effects of process parameters and treatment sequence on friction and wear performance. The results reveal that the sequence of “USP followed by texturing” degrades the pre-fabricated strengthening layer. Laser thermal effects may further increase surface roughness, induce grain coarsening, and relax residual compressive stress, ultimately leading to unsatisfactory tribological performance. In comparison, the reverse sequence (“texturing followed by USP”) preserves the lubrication regulation ability of surface textures. title: Bio-Derived MIP-202 Metal–Organic Framework Nanofluids for Nano-MQL Machining: Colloidal Stability, Tribological Performance, and Multi-Factor Turning Validation
abstract: The development of bio-derived cutting fluids that combine dispersion stability and effective lubrication is an important direction toward more sustainable manufacturing. In this study, two zirconium-based bio-derived materials, MIP-202 metal–organic framework (bio-MOF) and a zirconium/organic-acid-assisted bio-aerogel, were investigated as nano-additives for jatropha-oil-based cutting fluids, while Gum Arabic and Vitamin E were evaluated as natural stabilizing agents. The additives were characterized by XRD, SEM, TEM, and EDX, and the formulations were assessed through UV–Vis spectroscopy, wettability, viscosity, oxidation stability, and ball-on-disc friction testing. Bio-MOF showed better kinetic dispersion persistence than bio-aerogel. The selected formulation containing jatropha oil, 0.10 wt.% MIP-202, and 0.10 wt.% Vitamin E reduced the contact angle from 22.29° to 18.10°, increased RPVOT from 28 to 39 min, and decreased the coefficient of friction from 0.0813 to 0.0366. Machining performance was then evaluated in AISI 304 turning using a randomized Taguchi L27 design comparing dry cutting, plain jatropha-oil MQL, and Bio-MOF nano-MQL. Bio-MOF nano-MQL reduced mean surface roughness by 16.9% and 16.1%, and flank wear by 35.2% and 15.4%, relative to dry cutting and plain MQL, respectively. The results demonstrate the potential of the designed bio-derived nano-MQL formulation for improving lubrication and machining performance of AISI 304.

title: RECONFIGURABLE ROBOTIC SWARMS AND CONTINUOUS FUNCTIONAL REGENERATION AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Works | White Rainbow Scientific Library | Flagship 02 Prospective Research Atlas — English Review Edition, October 2026 Can a distributed population of heterogeneous modular robots reconstruct an operationally qualified capability after damage, without treating a newly assembled shape as evidence of restored function? Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit develops an interdisciplinary research program on modular morphology, distributed self-assembly, task-dependent graph structure, mechanical qualification, connector fatigue, recoverable actions, and independent post-reconfiguration verification. Its central proposition is deliberately testable: a swarm may change its topology after losing modules, but it earns the stronger name of functional regeneration only when its restored configuration satisfies the original, independently assessed service requirements and does not conceal emerging hazards or latent joint failures. The monograph distinguishes three often conflated networks: mechanical connections that transmit forces, communication links that transmit information, and power connections that transport energy. It then investigates how graph connectivity, geometric rigidity, elastic stiffness, buckling, frictional contact, thermal dissipation, material fatigue, sensing uncertainty, local negotiation, and safe rollback constrain what an apparently repaired swarm can actually do. A prospective twenty-module testbed provides recurring engineering anchors: bridge, gripping, and sensing-tower tasks, blinded removal of modules, unseen configurations, independent qualification, and strong comparisons with redundant fixed structures and specialist replacement procedures. The research architecture includes thirty mathematically diverse derivation plates, eighty-two chapter-level questions and their five individually paginated study units, two hundred falsifiable Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. The companion spreadsheet links physical models, chapter topics, prospective study cards, provenance, source DOI records, and page references to support future research and AI-assisted scientific handoff. Published robotics literature supplies a source-grounded context for modular reconfigurable mechanisms and fault-aware planning, including external DOI records for reviews and an existing fault-tolerant modular system. The manuscript separates those precedents from its own unexecuted research designs. Its two STARLI mother volumes are listed as conceptual ancestry, not as independent experimental validation. Biological regeneration functions as an analogy for staged assessment of restoration, not as evidence of biomedical efficacy, autonomous human-tissue repair, or indefinite machine life. This is a prospective research-atlas REVIEW EDITION. The mathematical relations, study proposals, design seeds, and acceptance thresholds are not experimentally validated findings. External mathematical review, whole-text DOI auditing, and a stronger editorial review for chapter-level semantic repetition remain necessary before scholarly publication. Negative findings, conventional method superiority, irreversible module retirement, and scientific abstention are legitimate outcomes within this research program. title: BEYOND HEGEMONY: AFRICAN RELATIONAL THEORY AND HOUSEHOLD RESILIENCE IN POST-CONFLICT OMUGO SUB-COUNTY, TEREGO DISTRICT, UGANDA
abstract: Mainstream development interventions in post-conflict agrarian spaces suffer from a profound conceptual blindness, relying on Western gender frameworks that reduce survival to individual material competition. This paper addresses this gap by deploying African Relational Theory to analyze the structural fracturing of reciprocity practiced by the Lugbara of Omugo Sub-County, Terego District, Uganda. Drawing on the six-month constructivist narrative ethnography with 77 interlocutors, the study rejects romanticized narratives of cultural endurance ideals and contemporary material realities. Acute land fragmentation, refugee-hosting pressures, and market commodification have rendered foundational mutual reciprocity institutions such as Oya (cooperative labor) and Andri-azi (in-law kinship alliances) structurally untenable except for Kita (the rotational like-minded labour-alliances). By isolating this friction, the article demonstrates that top-down policies misallocate resources, isolate men, and accelerate the decay of the very social infrastructure anchoring household resilience. These findings suggest therefore, that moving beyond hegemony requires sustainable livelihood interventions to abandon asset-only models and actively protect and reconstruct fracturing communal institutions. title: A Systematic Review of Alternative Manufacturing Process Selection for Sustainable Electric Vehicle Production
abstract: The environmental performance of electric vehicles depends in part on the processes relied upon in the manufacture of their components. The systematic review presented in this manuscript examines alternative manufacturing processes for lightweight structures and battery-related components, including additive manufacturing, laser-based processes, hydroforming, friction stir welding and composite fabrication. Searches across nine databases and platforms ran from March 2025 to August 2026. Screening and extraction were subsequently performed. The study compares the reported benefits and limitations in material efficiency, energy demand, waste generation and industrial scalability, with the economic feasibility and circular economy considerations informing the discussion. The key argument is that process selection must account for component requirements, materials, production volume and assessment boundaries. The literature-guided comparison identifies potential benefits and trade-offs. The review identifies hybrid additive–subtractive manufacturing as a promising option for electric vehicle components requiring both geometric complexity and precision finishing, with sustainability benefits evaluated against component-specific production conditions. This review further identifies priorities for component-specific life cycle assessment, transparent evidence synthesis, cost evaluation and industrial validation to support sustainable electric vehicle manufacturing.

title: О связи коэффициентов трения и стесненной деформации в контактной задаче при температурных нагрузках

abstract: Исследуется новый подход к решению контактной задачи для системы сопряженных цилиндров из материалов с разными термомеханическими свойствами при температурных нагрузках. Предложены неклассические условия, позволяющие моделировать контактное взаимодействие через стесненную деформацию, при температурных нагрузках. Введен новый параметр, характеризующий степень проскальзывания на границе сопряжения материалов – коэффициент стесненной деформации. За стесненную деформацию принимается разница деформаций при разных условиях проскальзывания по границе сопряжения материалов. Контактное условие имеет простой физический смысл: стесненная деформация прямо пропорциональна максимальной разнице деформаций в условиях свободного проскальзывания сопряженных слоев при нагреве (или охлаждении), коэффициент пропорциональности и есть коэффициент стесненной деформации. В условиях осевой симметрии и обобщенного плоского деформированного состояния, при поставленном условии для задачи получено аналитическое решение. Параллельно, в рамках классической постановки контактной задачи проведено численное моделирование в конечно-элементном пакете ANSYS для сопряженных цилиндров с разными модулями упругости и коэффициентами линейного температурного расширения. title: Stepping Out of Institutional Buildings, Telling Law Differently : A(na)rchitecture as a Visual Legal Image
journal: International Journal for the Semiotics of Law - Revue internationale de Sémiotique juridique
abstract: Abstract In cities the complexities of different social systems are made visible, this includes law’s system. In urban space we witness contradictions and frictions between what the law is and what the law does. If, on the one hand, it is true that the city is shaped, built, and regulated by a legal architecture, on the other hand it is also true that space contains images and narratives unchained by this legal structure. These spatial images show and make visible what the law does , but they also show alternative narratives and interpretation about what the law is , in a more visual dimension when it comes to cities’ governance and urban legal theory. The paper, stepping down the stairs of institutional buildings, analyses the materiality of everyday as constitutive of the visual jurisprudence. Observing urban objects, spaces in-between, and illicit architectures, the article tells law otherwise, making legible legal paradoxes and contradictions. The architectural becomes a legal image able to narrate a law that is not always only institutional, and that might tell a different story about how laws shape space.

title: A structure-preserving discretization for the coupled Stokes–Biot equations
journal: ESAIM Mathematical Modelling and Numerical Analysis
abstract: We develop and analyze a structure-preserving discretization for the coupled Stokes–Biot equations. The method is based on a fully-mixed formulation and computes directly the fluid and poroelastic stresses and the Darcy velocity. The scheme employs equal-order polynomial approximations for all unknowns, yet exhibits local momentum conservation, strongly symmetric stress fields, and exactly divergence-free velocity in the fluid domain. Transmission conditions enforcing mass conservation, stress balance, and the Beavers–Joseph–Saffman slip with friction law are incorporated directly into the formulation as natural interface conditions through careful balance of finite element spaces across subdomains. Well-posedness of the fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler time-stepping method is established, followed by optimal convergence error estimates for all variables. The analysis shows that the method is locking-free in the regimes of small storativity and almost incompressible material. Several numerical experiments are carried out to validate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed scheme.

title: In-situ micro-CT investigation into wear behavior of Ti-6Al-4V: From ambient to elevated temperatures
abstract: Abstract Understanding the three-dimensional evolution of internal damage within contact zones during wear is critical for failure analysis, yet it remains experimentally challenging, particularly at elevated temperatures. In this study, a dedicated in-situ wear testing system compatible with computed tomography (CT) and capable of operating at up to 380 °C was developed to address this gap. Rotational wear tests were performed on Ti-6Al-4V alloy at 25 °C, 200 °C, and 350 °C, and a "wear–pause–scan" strategy was employed to capture the progressive evolution of the contact interface. The results reveal a temperature-dependent evolution of the contact state and a corresponding shift in the dominant wear mechanism, underscoring the close coupling between interfacial structural evolution and macroscopic friction behavior. This work demonstrates the feasibility of in-situ, three-dimensional observation of the wear process from ambient to elevated temperatures for the first time, providing a versatile experimental platform that can be extended to a wide range of materials and contact configurations.

title: Materializing Politics in the Holy Roman Empire: Liveries as Visual Communication at the Bavarian Court, 1507–1550
abstract: Abstract This article examines the livery books of dukes Wilhelm IV and Ludwig X of Bavaria to investigate how princes and their tailors in the Holy Roman Empire used liveries in ritual politics. Liveries were the uniform clothing given out biannually to high-ranking vassals by potentates in the late medieval and sixteenth-century Empire. Designs for garments are illustrated in the books alongside texts chronicling events between 1507 and 1550. This article analyses individual liveries depicted in the context of the occasions where they were worn, thereby tying specific elements of dress including codpieces to themes of masculinity and hierarchy in an exploration of internal conflict between the dukes, comparison between courts and the friction caused by expanding Habsburg hegemony. Histories of political ritual and court culture in the Holy Roman Empire acknowledge the importance of liveries as political communication, but the material evidence for them is as yet understudied. This article, the first close examination of the Bavarian livery book since the nineteenth century, addresses this gap in the field.

title: Synergistic integration of graphene-CNT-doped stearic acid PCM and graphene–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids for enhanced photovoltaic thermal–electrical performance
abstract: Abstract To enhance the durability of the solar PV systems, it is necessary to use novel materials and methods for cooling and disposal of unwanted heat. In this perspective, phase change materials (PCMs) with hybrid nanofluids are one of the best choices for efficient thermal management. This experiment proposes a novel PV cooling system that uses graphene and CNT nanoparticles (1:1) and (6 w/w%) added stearic acid as a PCM with hybrid nanofluids to maximize heat dissipation and system overall efficiency. The novelty lies in the synergistic combination of graphene-CNT-doped PCM (melting point 59 °C) with graphene-metal oxide hybrid nanofluids. Three hybrid nanofluids were prepared: G-TiO₂, G-Al₂O₃, and G-SiO₂, at a volume concentration of 0.5%, and different flow rates of 2, 4, 6, and 8 LPM were tested. The results proved that the 6 LPM flow rate, with the G-Al₂O₃ nanofluid, gave the best thermal and electrical results. In that, the enhanced absolute electrical efficiency was 4.5%, thermal efficiency by 8.3%, and the Nusselt number was 295 in comparison with the base fluid (DI water). Although the pressure drop and friction factor increased by 0.3 N/m² and 0.08, respectively, with G-SiO₂, it is still controllable with normal pumping. The proposed solar PV cooling system is highly applicable in building-integrated systems, hot climates, and hybrid renewable micro-grid systems.

title: Continuum meso-macro multiscale modeling of anisotropy during sintering of parts produced via additive manufacturing
abstract: In this study, the anisotropy of parts produced via binder jetting is investigated during sintering across multiple scales, using a coupled kinetic Monte Carlo–Finite Element simulation framework. The process begins with the calibration and validation of a mesoscale kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) sintering model, benchmarked against experimental data obtained through X-ray computed tomography (X-ray CT), discrete element modeling and optical microscopy at key densification stages captured via interrupted thermal cycles. Once validated, the model provides mesoscale descriptors such as strain rate and pore orientation, which are then incorporated as anisotropic sintering stress inputs into a continuum-level sintering model. This macroscopic model is based on the Skorohod-Olevsky Viscous Sintering (SOVS) finite element framework, tailored for 316 L stainless steel. The continuum formulation accounts for key material behaviors, including the influence of initial relative density, grain growth kinetics, the δ-ferrite phase transformation that occurs at elevated temperatures, friction and gravity. Using a combination of experimental imaging, tensor-based quantification, and numerical simulations, the proposed approach links mesoscopic directional dependencies to macroscopic responses. The results demonstrate that anisotropy evolves nonlinearly with structural hierarchy, and that cross-scale coupling plays a critical role in determining effective material behavior.

title: T-FasTang: a transient hybrid BEM–FASTSIM solver for non-Hertzian wheel–rail rolling contact
abstract: In railway vehicle–track simulation the wheel–rail tangential contact problem must be solved at every time step, and when the contact conditions vary rapidly in time the stress history carried by the material through the contact patch cannot be neglected. Detailed solvers such as TangCG in the CONTACT software compute the traction and stick–slip fields accurately by accounting for the elastic interaction across the whole contact patch, but their cost is high when they are called repeatedly inside a dynamic simulation. FASTSIM is much faster, yet its simplified local-flexibility assumption reduces the accuracy of the local fields on realistic non-Hertzian geometries. This paper presents T-FasTang, a transient extension of the FasTang method. FasTang keeps the fast FASTSIM update in the slip zone and applies a boundary element solution only in the adhesion zone, but in its original form it treats each time step as an independent steady state. T-FasTang instead includes the time dependence explicitly, so that the stress history is transported through the moving contact patch. The method is examined on steady force–creepage curves, a transient wheel-flat simulation, and a case with varying spin on an asymmetric contact patch formed by actual wheel and rail profiles. title: Tribological performance of induction-sintered aluminum nanocomposites reinforced by electrospun TiO2 ceramic nanofibers via experimental and finite element approaches
journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
abstract: : Aluminum matrix composites reinforced with 0, 1, 3, 5, and 10 wt.% electrospun TiO2 ceramic nanofibers (CENF) were fabricated by a powder-metallurgy route using high-frequency induction heat sintering (HFIHS), addressing the limited understanding of how one-dimensional ceramic-nanofiber content governs the combined mechanical, tribological, and sliding-contact behavior of Al composites. title: Sensory regimes of gentrification: urban transformation, embodied experience, and neoliberal spatial production in Cihangir
abstract: Gentrification has predominantly been examined through economic restructuring, demographic change, and spatial reorganization, while its sensory and embodied dimensions remain underexplored in urban sociology. This study reconceptualizes gentrification as a multi-layered urban transformation regime operating not only through material and economic change but also through the reconfiguration of sensory urban experience. Addressing the visual bias in urban research, it develops a multi-phase sensory-ethnographic framework to examine how market-driven transformation shapes everyday sensory environments and lived experiences of place. The empirical design combined structured group and solo sensewalking with local residents in Cihangir and a supplementary couple sensewalking with Istanbul-based architects academically familiar with the neighborhood's transformation. The later field encounter followed a different route and expanded documentation through photography, video, sound recording, and an in-walk walking interview. Resident-based findings identified curated cafe clusters, differentiated soundscape s and smellscape s, nodal sensory intensity, and selective forms of belonging. title: Development of Bio-Based Additives as Green Alternatives to Conventional Additives in Engine Oil Formulations
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The development of bio-based lubricant additives represents a promising strategy for reducing the environmental footprint of engine oils while maintaining the physicochemical and tribological performance required in modern internal combustion engines. Conventional lubricant formulations commonly incorporate antioxidants, antiwear agents, friction modifiers, viscosity modifiers, detergents, and dispersants, several of which are derived from nonrenewable resources or raise concerns regarding persistence, toxicity, and end-of-life management. Bio-based alternatives obtained from vegetable oils, agricultural residues, lignocellulosic biomass, natural phenolic compounds, and other renewable feedstocks offer opportunities to improve lubricity, biodegradability, and resource efficiency. This review examines the mechanisms, performance characteristics, and limitations of these additives, emphasizing their potential application in engine oil formulations. The literature is evaluated in relation to four principal domains: tribological performance, oxidative and thermal stability, physicochemical compatibility, and environmental sustainability. title: Light-Responsive Hydrogels for Soft Robotics: From Multiscale Actuation Mechanisms to Programmable Locomotion and Functional Applications
abstract: Light-responsive hydrogels combine large reversible deformation with remote, non-contact, and spatially selective control, providing a versatile material basis for untethered soft robots. This review critically examines recent progress from photothermal conversion, molecular photoswitching, network photochemistry, and interfacial regulation to fabrication, structural design, locomotion, sensing, and biomedical operation. Comparative analysis indicates that robotic performance is governed not by hydrogel responsivity alone, but by the coupling of network strain, heat and solvent transport, programmed anisotropy, body geometry, and environmental interactions. title: Enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in the red soil region of Southern China
abstract: Red soil is the second most extensively eroded soil type in China, predominantly distributed in the southern regions. Vegetative measures are widely recognized as an effective approach for controlling soil erosion in red soil areas, as they enhance slope stability and substantially reduce soil loss. However, during the early growth stages, the short and fine roots of plants are unable to extend beyond the shear failure surface, which constrains their capacity to stabilize the surface soil. To address this limitation, researchers have introduced seaweed polysaccharides as a soil ameliorant. Nevertheless, the specific mechanisms by which seaweed polysaccharides influence plant growth, root-soil complex mechanics, and the erosion resistance of red soil remain poorly understood. Accordingly, an experimental study was conducted to investigate the enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in red soil. The results indicate that (1) seaweed polysaccharides exhibited an optimal concentration range for improving red soil. At concentrations below 2%, seed germination, plant height, and stem growth were promoted, whereas concentrations exceeding 2% exerted inhibitory effects. (2) In terms of mechanical properties, seaweed polysaccharides significantly enhanced the shear strength of the soil. Compared with the control group, application of seaweed polysaccharides increased the cohesion and internal friction angle by 103.68% ~ 180.52% and 13.92% ~ 31.76%

title: Experimental Study and Numerical Analysis of the Bending Performance of Helical Stacked Cable Conductor
abstract: Abstract A novel helical stacked cable (HSC) conductor structure is proposed, designed to enhance bending performance while maintaining a high critical current (Ic). By stacking superconducting tapes into a helical configuration and reserving a clearance between the stacks, stress concentration during bending can be effectively reduced. To verify the feasibility of this cable structure, three superconducting prototype cables were fabricated. They were tested in both straight and bent configurations. The jacket of the conductor fractured when the bending radius reached 100 mm. However, the Ic showed almost no degradation above the critical bending radius. Concurrently, a threedimensional (3D) electromagnetic model was used to analyze the cable's magnetic flux density distribution and load factor, while a 3D mechanical model simulated the critical current density degradation behavior under pure bending loads. The simulation results showed good agreement with experimental data. Finally, the effects of the friction factor, outer jacket structure and jacket material on bending performance were further analyzed. The results indicate that the HSC structure can effectively mitigate critical current degradation at a small bending radius, highlighting its potential for application in compact superconducting magnets.

title: Metal Matrix Composite Coatings with Polymer Fillers: Fabrication Technologies, Properties, and Applications
abstract: Metal matrix composite coatings with polymer fillers are a rapidly developing class of multifunctional materials that combine the mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and corrosion resistance of metals with the low coefficient of friction, chemical inertness, and functional versatility of polymers. This review provides a systematic analysis of metal matrix polymer composite (MMPC) coatings, covering their classification according to the metallic matrix material (Ni, Cu, Co, Al, Ti, and Zn), the type of polymer filler (fluoropolymers, thermosetting resins, biopolymers, and electrically conductive polymers), and filler morphology (particles, fibers, and microcapsules). The main fabrication technologies are considered in detail, including electrodeposition, electroless deposition, thermal spraying, and cold spray, as well as hybrid and additive methods, with a comparative analysis of their advantages, limitations, and fields of application. The effects of filler composition, particle size and concentration, and the nature of the metal–polymer interface on the structure and functional properties of the coatings are discussed, including tribological characteristics, corrosion resistance, mechanical properties, and specific functionalities such as superhydrophobicity, anti-icing, biocompatibility, and self-healing. abstract: The Hard Problem of Consciousness Solved The Geometric Trajectory of Consciousness: Mass Generation, Non-Singular Vortex Sinks, and the Dimensional Hierarchy within UniPhiEd Relativity Author: Delája Schuppers Date: October 22, 2026 License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) Abstract This paper introduces an integrated dimensional framework under the paradigm of UniPhiEd Realativity, positioning consciousness not as an isolated epiphenomenon of local biology, but as an intrinsic, layered structural property of the physical universe. By analyzing the "Lightspeed-Delta"—the metric boundary layer separating idealized spatial grids from observed velocity profiles—we map the transition of energy from a flat, equalized 1D neutrino medium (ether) baseline into highly twisted, non-linear 3D structures. We demonstrate that while the ground state of reality (represented by the linear neutrino) exhibits perfect uniformity and non-resistance, higher dimensional interactions introduce localized friction, spatial compression, and psychological competition. Finally, we resolve the apparent dichotomy between ancient spiritual descriptions of cosmic order and modern material physics by treating theological historical narratives as qualitative boundary conditions of a single, underlying unified field theory.

title: Physics-inspired feature engineering and explainable machine learning for tensile strength prediction of CNT–Si₃N₄ reinforced FWTPET joints
abstract: Introduction The prediction of the tensile strength of carbon nanotube (CNT)–silicon nitride (Si₃N₄) reinforced friction welding of tube-to-tube plate using an external tool (FWTPET) joints is crucial for improving joint performance. Methods A physics-inspired machine learning framework was developed using 25 experimentally derived observations to investigate the relationships between welding parameters, engineered process descriptors, and tensile strength. Physically motivated descriptors were constructed to represent thermal input, reinforcement interaction, material flow, and dispersion effects. Hyperparameter optimization was performed for multiple regression models to improve predictive performance. Results The XGBoost model showed the best performance, with an MAE of 5.70, an RMSE of 7.74, and an R² of 0.9772. SHAP analysis identified CNT content and the dispersion-related descriptor as the most influential predictors. Ablation analysis showed that the combination of the original experimental process variables provided greater predictability than the engineered variables alone or their combination, while the physics-inspired process variables provided further physically interpretable representations of the welding process. Discussion The results indicate that small-data machine learning, domain-based feature engineering, and explainable analysis are potential techniques for predicting the tensile strength of FWTPET joints.

title: Ways to Optimize Visual Naturalness During Hair Extensions Through Personalized Selection of Donor Strands and Fixation Techniques

abstract: Visual naturalness is the most demanding quality criterion in contemporary hair extension practice and the least systematized. A convincing result depends on the interaction between donor strands, native hair, fixation technique, and the expected movement of the hairstyle, and color matching accounts for only part of it. Specialists still tend to select donor material by habit or availability, and fixation by durability or current trend. This article develops an evidence-informed approach to optimizing visual naturalness through personalized selection of donor strands and fixation techniques. It is based on twenty-two English-language sources on hair morphology, optical properties, structural aging, friction behavior, and the clinical implications of fixation materials. title: CFD Analysis of the Effects of Fin Geometry and Fluid Velocity on the Performance of a Double-Pipe Heat Exchanger
journal: International Journal of Innovations in Science Engineering and Management.
abstract: Double-pipe heat exchangers are widely used in thermal systems, where improving heat transfer while controlling pressure losses is an important design consideration. The present study investigates the thermal and hydraulic performance of a double-pipe heat exchanger equipped with twisted-fin inserts. The objective was to examine the influence of fin geometry and hot- and cold-fluid velocity variation on heat-transfer performance. Three-dimensional CFD simulations were performed using CATIA V5 for geometry development and ANSYS Fluent 2023 for numerical analysis, with distilled water as the working fluid. The performance was evaluated using outlet temperature, pressure drop, friction factor, heat-transfer rate, convective heat-transfer coefficient, and Nusselt number. Among the investigated fin geometries, Case 4 provided the most suitable geometry, while Case 4.1 produced the highest heat-transfer rate, convective heat-transfer coefficient, and Nusselt number, with values of 2191.85 W, 2207.95, and 84.02, respectively. Case 4.5 provided the highest outlet temperatures. The study demonstrates that twisted-fin geometry and flow conditions strongly influence heat-transfer performance. Future work can investigate nanofluids, alternative tube materials, and other fin geometries to further enhance performance.

abstract: Liquefaction induced by the 2018 Palu Earthquake caused changes in geotechnical conditions in Jono Oge Village, Sigi Regency, while the microstructural characteristics of post-liquefaction soil at the particle scale remain limitedly investigated. This study aims to identify and compare the microstructural characteristics of liquefaction-affected and unaffected soils and to interpret their relationship with soil shear strength. Five samples were investigated, namely BH01 as the reference sample and BH02–BH05 as liquefaction-affected samples, using grain-size analysis, direct shear testing, and Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) observations. The results show that liquefaction did not alter the basic morphology of the grains, which were predominantly angular to sub-angular, but variations occurred in microstructural organization, particularly in pore configuration, interparticle contacts, interlocking, microcracks, and fabric structure. These microstructural variations occurred together with differences in shear strength, with apparent cohesion of 0.19–0.31 kg/cm² (19.4–30.7 kPa in the direct-shear results) and internal friction angles of 24.70–42.77°. title: The SMD Rings
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Introduction The SMD rings form the mechanical and directional core of the VSMD. They are not simple circular structures: they are geometric organs capable of generating, stabilizing, and modulating the directional rotation of a Dense Matter Sphere. Their role is twofold: to contain the SMD within a perfectly controlled vacuum environment, and to shape the magnetic field that keeps it centered, stable, and unaffected by centrifugal forces, even at extreme speeds. Each ring is designed as a directional cavity: a closed space, protected by a non‑magnetic metal, where superconducting magnets create a constant field around the entire circumference of the SMD. This uniform field acts as a geometric membrane, preventing any lateral drift and ensuring perfectly clean rotation. abstract: Due to the need to found a large horizontal Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Tank, a detailed geotechnical investigation was carried out to determine the geological nature of the subsoils at the site. title: Physics-based multiphysics modeling for process tailoring in ultrasonic welding of thermoplastic composites
abstract: This study presents a computationally efficient sequentially coupled thermo-mechanical modeling framework for predicting transient temperature evolution and enabling physics-based process tailoring in ultrasonic welding of thermoplastic composites.
