title: Analytical rolling force model for hot rolling of wide-thick clad plates using a novel variable-trajectory cosine unified yield criterion
abstract: Abstract During the hot rolling of wide-thick clad plates, precise prediction of the rolling force is considered critical for ensuring interfacial bonding integrity, achieving uniform deformation, and optimizing process parameters. Most existing rolling-force models are based on the Mises yield criterion, which constrains their capacity to reliably characterize mechanical behavior under complex stress states. To resolve this issue, a variable-trajectory cosine unification yield criterion is developed. An adjustable parameter is introduced into this criterion, allowing a unified representation of classical yield criteria including Tresca, Mises, and twin shear stress, and enabling accurate prediction of the yield characteristics of various metallic materials subjected to various stress paths. Based on the variable-trajectory cosine unified yield criterion, an analytical rolling force model applicable to the hot rolling of wide-thick clad plates is established. The friction factor, base-thickness ratio, and interfacial stress distribution are comprehensively incorporated into the model, and the predictive accuracy of the model is validated through multi-pass hot rolling experiments. The overall prediction error is maintained within 5%, and the mean absolute error is reduced by 11.22 percentage points relative to the conventional Mises model. title: A Process-Informed, Photorealistic Digital Twin for Vision-Based Inline Inspection of C-SMC Strip Deposition
abstract: Inline quality assurance for Sheet Molding Compound (SMC) manufacturing is hindered by the lack of large-scale, accurately labeled image datasets for training machine-learning models. This work presents a process-informed, photorealistic digital twin for carbon-fiber SMC strip deposition. A rigid-body simulation reproduces the deposition kinematics (settling, friction, belt motion), while a physically grounded polarization-rendering model produces realistic appearance, so that every image carries exact, mutually consistent labels in synchronized formats: oriented bounding boxes, point annotations, density maps, and polarization renderings (Angle and Degree of Linear Polarization). Because the joint distribution of many overlapping strips cannot be specified analytically, simulation yields exact, scalable ground truth that manual annotation cannot provide. The twin produces over 16,000 images across 3,300 frames, and the synthetic data replicate near-isotropic fiber orientation (axial concentration r < 0.05) consistent with as-deposited commercial SMC. title: Experimental Study of Surface Reinforcement of Soil Slopes Using Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Stabilized Soil
abstract: Rainfall-induced erosion and deformation of soil slopes remain important concerns for long-term slope stability, highlighting the need for effective surface reinforcement methods. This study experimentally investigated the mechanical and rainfall-resistant performance of carbon fiber-reinforced stabilized soil for slope surface protection. Four soil types were initially evaluated using unconfined compression tests with different Eco Soil Binder (E.S.B.) contents, and well-graded sand (SW) with 20% E.S.B. was selected for further testing. Carbon fiber contents ranging from 0 to 1.2% were considered; however, stable specimens could not be formed at 1.2%, while 0.6% provided the highest compressive strength among the valid test conditions. The selected mixture of SW, 20% E.S.B., and 0.6% carbon fiber was further characterized through triaxial compression tests, yielding an apparent cohesion of 0.152 MPa and a friction angle of 37.23°. Artificial rainfall tests were then conducted using 1:50 geometrically scaled slope models with berm lengths of 0.05 and 0.15 m under a rainfall intensity of 20 mm/h for 48 h. title: Balancing densification and MAX-phase stability in FAST/SPS Al–Ti₃SiC₂ composites
journal: Archives of Civil and Mechanical Engineering
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the microstructural evolution and interfacial stability of FAST/SPS-processed Al–10 wt% Ti₃SiC₂ composites consolidated at temperatures between 500 and 600 °C. Microstructural characterization by SEM, TEM and STEM-EDS revealed progressive densification of the aluminum matrix with increasing temperature, accompanied by improved particle bonding and stable incorporation of the Ti₃SiC₂ reinforcement. The relative density increased from 92.4% at 500 °C to 99.1% at 600 °C, while hardness increased from 46 HV1 to ~ 55 HV1. TEM and STEM-EDS analyses further revealed localized interfacial features at elevated temperatures, including Ti-containing phases and local Si-rich regions near the matrix–particle interface, while the Ti₃SiC₂ reinforcement largely retained its structural integrity. Mechanical testing showed a systematic increase in compressive stress with sintering temperature, reaching ~ 525 MPa at 50% strain for the composite sintered at 600 °C. Tribological performance was strongly influenced by microstructural evolution and densification: materials processed at 500–520 °C exhibited severe adhesive-delamination wear associated with residual porosity, whereas samples sintered at 560–580 °C showed stable friction behaviour and predominantly mild abrasive wear. title: Current-driven Magnetic Skyrmions for Encoding/Storing Information: Manipulation and Dynamics in Nanoscale Structures
abstract: This dissertation investigates the dynamics of current-driven magnetic skyrmions, topological solitons in magnetic materials with broken spatial inversion symmetry, for low-power spintronic applications like racetrack memory and multilevel data storage. Skyrmions’ small size and low driving current requirements make them promising information carriers. The research examines skyrmion motion under driving currents, pinning effects, and thermal fluctuations, using numerical simulations (Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation), analytical studies (Thiele equation), and theoretical modeling to design novel data storage devices. The study analyzes skyrmion motion amidst pinning potentials from material imperfections. Simulations reveal that thermal fluctuations vary with damping: acting as a frictional force at low damping or a driving force aiding depinning at high damping. The Thiele equation quantifies this, though its accuracy wanes at low temperatures with pinning. The skyrmion Hall angle, influenced by current and pinning, provides insights for ambient-condition devices. These findings underpin a proposed multilevel data storage device, where controlled current positions skyrmions at pinning sites for high-density, low-power encoding. The research also explores altermagnetic (ATM) skyrmions, which exhibit d-wave symmetry via exchange-driven spin splitting. title: Modeling Interfacial Temperature Distribution to Enhance Machining Condition Optimization
journal: The American Journal of Engineering And Technology
abstract: Temperature distribution at the tool–workpiece interface is a critical factor governing machining performance, tool wear, surface integrity, and process stability. During metal cutting, plastic deformation, friction, and heat transfer generate complex thermal fields that vary with cutting speed, feed rate, depth of cut, tool geometry, and lubrication conditions. Accurate estimation of these fields is challenging because the cutting interface is difficult to access directly, while individual measurement techniques provide incomplete or spatially limited information. This paper develops a theoretical and computational framework for modeling interfacial temperature distribution and integrating thermal predictions into machining-condition optimization. The proposed approach combines transient heat-transfer equations, a moving heat-source representation, tool–workpiece thermal interaction, numerical simulation, and experimental validation through infrared thermography and tool–workpiece thermocouple measurements. Inverse heat-transfer analysis is considered for estimating inaccessible interface temperatures from measurable thermal responses. The framework also incorporates machining performance indicators, including surface roughness, residual stress, and thermal loading, to support multi-objective parameter selection. title: Seismic Performance of Prefabricated Steel–Timber Hybrid Joint: Experimental and Numerical Study
abstract: Existing steel–timber structures may exhibit limited composite action between the two materials. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel sleeve-connected prefabricated steel–timber (SCPST) beam–column joint that utilizes steel sleeves and high-strength bolts for assembly. To assess its seismic performance, five full-scale interior joint specimens with different beam-sleeve thicknesses and lengths were tested under low-cycle reversed loading. The experimental results revealed that deformation and damage were concentrated at the beam ends, whereas the timber columns remained essentially elastic, satisfying the strong-column–weak-beam seismic design objectives. Within the tested specimen matrix, the peak load of the specimen with an 8 mm beam-sleeve thickness was 43.75% higher than that of the 4 mm specimen, while that of the specimen with a 400 mm sleeve length was 17.46% higher than that of the 300 mm specimen. Frictional slip at the timber–steel interfaces and yielding of the stiffeners were identified as the primary energy-dissipation mechanisms. Simplified analytical expressions based on Eurocode 3 and Chinese timber design provisions were developed to evaluate three potential beam-end failure modes, and the calculated resistances differed from the experimental results by less than 10%. abstract: Abstract. Discrete element modeling (DEM) provides a methodology for simulating the dynamics of sea ice from fracture through post-failure granular behavior. Because the approach is designed explicitly to represent the cohesive or frictional forces between distinct floes, it may offer a better representation than continuum-based approaches for some phenomena. Propagation of cracks can depend as much on the characteristics of post-failure element contacts as intact ones. So, distinct parameters are introduced to the contact physics in this model to provide control of the failure rate and timing of transitions in contact response and to constrain the amount of energy and momentum transfer in the contact failure process. title: Crafting post-growth? A support-structure diagnosis of Jaipur’s craft economy
abstract: Post-growth scholarship has often celebrated craft as a privileged site for imagining postcapitalist and post-growth transitions. Yet this discussion remains largely Global North-centred and empirically underdeveloped, drawing mostly on small-scale, elective and niche craft economies rather than large craft sectors where artisanal labour constitutes a major livelihood system. This paper addresses this gap through the case of Jaipur’s craft economy, one of the world’s largest concentrated craft economies. The study draws on semi-structured interviews with craft-sector experts, field visits to craft fairs and markets, participant observation at a socio-ecological enterprise, and documentary analysis conducted between 2023 and 2024. We examine how Jaipur’s craft sector enables, constrains and complicates post-growth-compatible forms of territorial development. To do so, we develop a support-structure diagnosis, understood as an analysis of the institutional, material, financial, cultural, geographical and historical conditions sustaining, transforming or absorbing craft economies into dominant growth-oriented circuits. We map three interrelated support structures operating across multiple scales: top-down institutional structures, bottom-up and intermediary structures, and local conditions. abstract: Thin-walled aluminium castings, such as stator housings for electric motors, are susceptible to distortion during and after machining due to the superposition of residual stress states introduced by casting, heat treatment and cutting. title: Porous PDMS/SrTiO3 Composite Triboelectric Nanogenerators toward Self-Powered Information Encoding and Intelligent Gesture Recognition
abstract: Abstract Rapid advances in wearable human–machine interaction (HMI) and internet of things (IoT) systems are severely limited by the short service life, poor mechanical conformability, and environmental drawbacks of conventional battery-powered sensing devices. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a compelling self-powered sensing alternative, yet real-world deployment is hindered by insufficient surface charge density and inadequate mechanical compliance of prevailing polymer friction layers. Herein, we adopt a facile sacrificial salt template strategy to fabricate flexible, three-dimensionally interconnected porous polydimethylsiloxane/strontium titanate (PDMS/SrTiO3) composite films for simultaneously boosting triboelectric output performance and mechanical compliance. The interconnected porous architecture greatly enlarges the effective contact area and improves elastic deformability of the active layer, while uniformly dispersed high-dielectric SrTiO3 nanoparticles reinforce dielectric polarization and interfacial charge retention. The optimized dual-structured TENG (DS-TENG) delivers a peak open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 178 V and a maximum power density of 450 mW/m2, retaining stable electrical stability over 20,000 continuous contact-separation cycles. Leveraging the high signal fidelity of DS-TENG, we demonstrate a wearable self-powered Morse code communication system, which encodes all 26 Latin alphabet letters from finger flexion-derived electrical signals. journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: The concept of “full-domain propped fracturing” aims to improve fracture placement morphology by efficient placement in main fractures and hierarchical propping of multi-scale fractures, thereby effectively addressing the limitation of propped fracture volume in unconventional oil and gas reservoirs. Using proppant-fiber clusters instead of pure proppant as the basic transport units in fractures can effectively increase the lateral migration distance and vertical placement height of proppant in main fractures, serving as a key technical approach for achieving efficient fracture placement. This study constructed a physical model of proppant-fiber clusters through microstructural observations, static settling experiments, and dynamic transport experiments, and revealed the settling and placement patterns of cluster units within fractures. The results indicated that proppant-fiber clusters were a composite system jointly composed of a fiber framework that traps proppant particles, a filamentous network of friction reducer polymers, and sheet-like stabilizer structures. Characterization of cluster units and their size distributions revealed that increasing fiber mass fraction and length facilitated the formation of larger cluster units. abstract: This paper presents the conceptual design and operational principles of a Toroidal Electromagnetic Levitation Vehicle, an innovative transport system that merges magnetic levitation (maglev) with a closed-loop toroidal geometry. By eliminating traditional mechanical friction and wheel-rail contact, the vehicle achieves high-speed propulsion with significantly reduced energy losses and acoustic emissions. Key findings from our preliminary simulations indicate that the toroidal configuration optimizes spatial efficiency, enables continuous high-speed looping without traditional terminal turnaround delays, and enhances passenger safety through inherent centrifugal stabilization and fail-safe magnetic braking. This research highlights the potential of toroidal maglev architectures as a scalable, sustainable paradigm for future urban and inter-city mass transit networks.

title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO 2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

title: Eddy-Current Brake Dynamometer Hysteresis in Engineering Technology Education Test Beds: A Torque-Reference Calibration Linking Magnetic Saturation to Load-Setting Repeatability Bounds
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Eddy-current brake dynamometers are widely used in engineering technology education as load-setting test beds, yet their torque output exhibits hysteresis that is rarely quantified against a traceable reference. The framework treats the brake as a saturable magnetic circuit and derives a closed-form expression for the hysteresis loop width as a function of excitation current, disc permeability and air-gap reluctance. A calibration protocol is specified in which a reference torque arm and a strain-gauge load cell establish the ascending and descending torque-current branches, from which a repeatability bound is computed at the 95% coverage level. The analysis is methodological and does not report empirical measurements; instead, it formalises the conditions under which hysteresis becomes the dominant contributor to load-setting uncertainty and derives the excitation range over which the bound remains within a stated tolerance. The principal contribution is a design-stage procedure that allows educators and technicians to predict whether a given eddy-current dynamometer can meet a specified repeatability target before a laboratory exercise is commissioned. The framework is intended to support the accreditation of test beds used in mechanical and electrical engineering technology curricula.
